To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) HIV-1 RNA is detectable in lymphoid tissue in patients on effective antiretrovial treatment, (2) the amount of HIV-1 associated with follicular dendritic is the best predictor of plasma HIV RNA levels, (3) viral load in lymphocytes is a poor predictor of plasma viral load, (4) the amount of virus associated with follicular dentritic cells decreases with time on treatment, but (5) the amount of residual virus in lymphocytes
plasma and tissue HIV-1 RNA and p24 levels decrease by 3 log10 during combination antirevetroviral therapy in early, asymptomatic infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantitative analysis of human immune-deficiency virus-1 in lymphoid tissues of patients with early, untreated HIV infection, as well as in patients with early, treated HIV infection.
the quantitative analysis of HIV-1 in lymphoid tissue in early HIV-1 infection before and during treatment.
the quantitative analysis of the HIV-1 response in lymphoid tissue to combination antiretro-viral therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lymphoid tissue viral load is a marker of residual HIV-1 replication, which is only suppressed to undetectable levels by combination therapy.
the combination of HAART and the immune system is able to control HIV-1 replication and to prevent progression to AIDS in patients with HIV infection.
treatment with combination therapy is associated with a marked decrease of HIV-1 p 24 antigen and HIV-1 mRNA in lymphoid tissues of patients with early HIV-1 infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the treatment response in lymphoid tissue is delayed and incomplete, and that tissue viral load is not a good marker to assess the efficacy of antiretrovials in the treatment of HIV-1 infection.
treatment-induced decline of HIV-1 p 24 and HIV- 1 RNA in lympho id tissue was delayed compared to the decrease of plasma viral load.
the viral load in lymph node tissue is not only a marker of the infection but that the tissue viral load may be an independent prognostic factor for progression to AIDS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV replication is not fully suppressed in lymphoid tissue in the absence of detectable viral replication in plasma.

HIV-1 replication in the lymphoid tissue of early infected patients can be efficiently controlled by treatment, but that the residual viral replication that is observed in the tissue even during full plasma viral suppression may contribute to the persistence of viral reservoirs in the tissue.
HIV-1 RNA and p24 in tissue are not only a marker of viral reservoir, they can also be used as an indicator of the effectiveness of treatment in the early stages of HIV-1 disease.
